page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Ant." (printed as small capitals "Anᴛ."), "aduersatur" (printed "aducrsatur"), "inaunl-" at the line end, and the heading "PRÆFATIO ÆVSCVLTATI-onis fecunda." (the line break and second line are hard to read; the second line has an uncertain reading and may be a subtitle). The first line starts with a fragment "benter" that continues from the previous page. The printed text "Iouis igitur" and "(Nam dupla Dionysi" appear to be parts of the same paragraph but may be printed in separate lines. Small marks and specks along the left and right edges and below the text are not printed text and are left out. The Greek and Latin spelling of "Dionyfum" and "Dionysus" follows the printed form, which shows long s. The word "tem" at the end of a line is not used.
